title: Define and verify quality in the same Saga
statement: As a quality engineer or reviewer, I can define independently reviewable test cases with ordered expected behavior, link them to requirements, and inspect current verification evidence without leaving the Saga.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Each test case has stable identity, immutable definition revisions, append-only lifecycle history, and explicit conflict heads.
A test revision records ordered steps with stable step IDs, actions, per-step expected results, and an overall expected result; removed step IDs are not reused for different behavior.
Tests explicitly declare positive, negative, and edge coverage kinds, while criterion policy identifies which kinds are required for readiness.
A current test-case relation links directly to one or more criteria and pins both the test revision and story revision.
Quality evidence distinguishes test-implementation diffs, implementation-under-test references, and execution artifacts; implementation references exactly match current Item-owned selectors.
A satisfying run has one semantic head, a passed result, the current test revision, the active source comparison identity, and resolved current evidence.
Queries derive Requirements to Quality to Diff paths and compare design, implementation, and quality coverage per criterion without collapsing them into one score.
Quality > Test Cases lists each case as an independent page using the same concise title, description, expected behavior, and collapsed-history pattern as stories.
